QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_15

question.text: Purvanchal Special Situations Fund seeks to enter a Dissolution Period after its Liquidation Period expires. Under SEBI's April-2024 framework, the Dissolution Period cannot exceed:

answer.text: The original tenure of the scheme, with no further extension
It is open-ended until all assets are monetised

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI Circular 26-Apr-2024 caps the Dissolution Period at NO MORE than the ORIGINAL TENURE of the scheme and explicitly prohibits any further extension after expiry. Entry requires 75% LP consent and filing of an Information Memorandum with a merchant banker's due-diligence certificate before liquidation-period expiry. The Trap: 1 year confuses with the Liquidation Period. '2 years / 2/3rd' repurposes the tenure-extension rule. 'Open-ended' is flat wrong. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C unique — post-2024 regulatory content not in older Distributor curriculums. Manager's Pro-Tip: File the IM with the merchant banker at least 45 days before liquidation-period expiry — SEBI's informal feedback window alone consumes 2-3 weeks. No fresh commitments or new investments are permitted during the Dissolution Period.
